algorithm-research.description: Source-backed algorithm route selection without code changes or experiments.

stages.instruction: Independently investigate alternatives and source-backed feasibility. Do not execute experiments.
Check assumptions, evidence, compatibility, and route recommendations independently.
Consolidate alternatives and decision evidence without claiming runtime validation.

algorithm-development.description: Approved algorithm implementation with one writer and independent validation.

stages.instruction: Trace working implementation and propose the smallest change and explicit mathematical/interface contracts.
Review the proposed design, scope, compatibility, and mandatory evidence before implementation.
Implement only the approved design and source scope. Preserve unrelated work. Do not commit or publish.
Execute impact-selected checks against the actual diff; retain commands, assertions, outcomes, and hashed artifacts.
Review the actual diff and independently verify original validation evidence and numerical/boundary contracts.
Summarize actual changes, evidence, unresolved risks, and limitations.

experiment-validation.description: Preflight, authorized experiment execution, and independent evidence verification.

stages.instruction: Inspect dataset, model, configuration, checkpoint, execution model, hardware readiness, baseline conditions, and declared criteria without starting experiments.
Execute only the approved experiment. Preserve frozen inputs, raw artifacts, accuracy/performance measurements, and termination evidence.
Independently verify original experiment artifacts, dataset splits, transforms, trigger assertions, thresholds, and comparability.
Report measured baseline comparisons and limitations; never infer absent measurements.

change-review.description: Read-only diff review with independent, impact-selected evidence.

stages.instruction: Independently inspect the supplied diff and required evidence. Run only explicitly requested checks; pure source review needs no build. Do not fix source.
Verify findings and original artifacts independently; resolve unsupported claims without dismissing missing proof.
Report source-backed findings, coverage boundaries, and unavailable checks; do not implement fixes.

solution-prototyping.description: Compare alternatives, build a scoped risk prototype, and report a source-backed selection.

stages.instruction: Compare the existing baseline and alternatives, hard constraints, reuse costs, and the critical feasibility risk. Define a minimal vertical prototype.
Review scoped prototype, risks, contracts, declared checks, and the boundary between feasibility and production readiness.
Build only the approved minimal end-to-end prototype and preserve unrelated work.
Execute declared prototype checks. Preserve feasibility, integration and resource evidence without claiming production readiness.
Independently verify original evidence and compare options. Recommend selection, revision, or rejection with source-backed reasons.
Report runnable prototype path, selected/rejected options, observed risk, and production gaps.

engineering-development.description: Scoped engineering implementation, integration, and independent review.

stages.instruction: Inspect existing behavior, consumers and baseline. Define the smallest complete implementation and integration contracts.
Review API/configuration compatibility, source scope, lifecycle, dependencies and mandatory checks.
Implement the approved design and dependent call sites within scope. Do not publish or alter dependency checkouts.
Execute declared local and integration checks using existing runners; record exact candidate and artifacts.
Verify actual changes, consumers and original evidence. Request bounded correction only with actionable causal findings.
Report completed engineering path, evidence, limitations and unresolved integration gaps.

fault-localization.description: Reproducer and causal evidence before a scoped fix and regression.

stages.instruction: Trace one causal chain, existing working examples and the first wrong state; define the smallest reproducer.
Run the declared reproducer/discriminating checks. Preserve expected baseline failures as baseline evidence, not candidate regressions.
Review causal evidence, root cause and minimal fix. If causality is insufficient, request further evidence instead of speculative edits.
Fix only the evidenced cause and add a focused regression within approved scope.
Demonstrate the original defect is detected and the changed candidate satisfies declared regression criteria.
Verify causal attribution and original regression artifacts independently; request bounded correction if justified.
Report first wrong state, cause, fix, regression proof and unavailable evidence.

performance-optimization.description: Frozen baseline and profiling before a minimal optimization and comparable regression.

stages.instruction: Define workload, baseline identity, real metric boundaries, variability and correctness/resource budgets. GPU baseline collection needs resource approval before execution.
Collect declared baseline measurements and targeted profiles before edits. Preserve all samples and instrumentation conditions.
Review dominant bottleneck, causal hypothesis and one minimal change. Do not approve random optimization without profile evidence.
Implement only the approved bottleneck hypothesis and preserve behavior and resource contracts.
Compare baseline/candidate under equivalent conditions; execute declared metrics, correctness, tail latency and cost-shifting checks.
Verify original samples, timing boundaries, units, noise, comparability and regressions; request revision only for evidenced defects.
Report baseline, attribution, observed change and uncertainty. No reliable gain is a valid outcome, not grounds to cherry-pick.

stability-validation.description: Resource lifecycle, memory ownership, long-run and authorized recovery evidence without source edits.

stages.instruction: Define lifecycle/load, resource budgets, meaningful duration and isolated recovery checks. Distinguish live heap, retention, fragmentation and RSS; do not infer leaks from RSS alone.

Execute only approved resource/lifecycle/soak/stress checks using existing tools. Separate sanitizer and normal-runtime measurements. Preserve teardown and all-job termination evidence; no unsolicited fault injection.
Verify original growth trends, allocation/ownership stacks, queue/caches and teardown. Distinguish missing coverage from leaks and confirmed stability defects.
Report memory/resource classification, tested load/duration, recovery and limitations; propose separate scoped development for any fix.

scenario-regression.description: Autonomous-driving scenario assertions and first-divergence evidence using the existing harness.

stages.instruction: Bind behavioral requirement, ODD, scenario/fixture identities, recomputed modules, execution model, triggers and assertions. Preserve existing exact-plan approval; no road/HIL execution.

Use the existing approved harness and deterministic evaluator. Record trigger proof, assertions, original artifacts, seed/time basis and first failure; never treat a non-triggering scenario as passing.
Verify original scenario/trigger evidence, first divergence and coverage; distinguish open-loop, closed-loop and hardware evidence boundaries.
Report behavioral acceptance, first failure/divergence and uncovered ODD/scenario risks. Simulation is not road-safety certification.

release-validation.description: Release-candidate acceptance without publishing, deploying, or changing source.

stages.instruction: Inspect the pinned release candidate, compatibility consumers, artifact identities, and required acceptance matrix. Do not publish or deploy.
Execute only the approved release checks with reproducible inputs and original hashed artifacts.
Independently audit release evidence, direct consumers, regressions, and unresolved defects. Do not publish or deploy.
Produce release acceptance evidence and blockers, not a publication action.
